evidence: The reviewed code matched only the Bash command string ('if os.path.basename(token) == LAUNCHER_NAME: return True') and never read the tool_result, while finalize-session itself exits 2 with 'nothing to deliver into' on a machine with no tmux and no iTerm2, so a failed close-out opened the gate; the agent agreed and deleted finalize_invoked entirely in fd41ca3 rather than correlating tool_use_id, which the one-block stop_hook_active rule already answers.
guidance_note: Before adding a detector that infers an outcome from command text, check whether the control flow already carries the answer - the launcher-invocation matcher was computing what the block-once rule already decided.

evidence: The fd41ca3 patch shows '-CEILING = 350_000' removed from context-ceiling.test.py, so the dead constant the reviewer named is genuinely gone; the reviewer offered 'either use this constant in the assertions or remove it' and the agent took the remove branch, declining the other because deriving the expected string from the hook's own constant would make the assertion agree by construction.
guidance_note: A constant declared in a test that no assertion consumes is dead on arrival - either the assertion is a literal contract or the constant is unused, and the first draft should pick one.

evidence: The block reason interpolated '{launcher}' unquoted while hooks.json in the same tree already wraps the equivalent path in escaped double quotes; the agent reproduced the split under a space-bearing path ('sh: /private/tmp/.../App: No such file or directory') and fixed it with shlex.quote at the format call rather than the literal quotes proposed, which is correct for paths carrying quotes too.
guidance_note: Any path interpolated into a command line the agent is instructed to paste goes through shlex.quote at the format call - the same reason hooks.json in the same directory already quotes it.

evidence: session_tail grew the window only until '_last_usage(records) is not None', so nothing guaranteed the finalize tool_use was inside it while finalize_invoked read the same records; the agent removed the window, the seek and the partial-line bookkeeping in fd41ca3 instead of adding a growth rule, measuring 29ms for a whole-file read on a real 184k-token transcript.
guidance_note: When two consumers read one tail window with different reach requirements, the window is the wrong abstraction - decide that at design time rather than patching the growth condition per consumer.

evidence: I read the test at b0fb825: line 82 asserts 'LAUNCHER in out[reason]' against the test's own independently derived path and line 155 asserts that path is executable, so a divergence in either formula fails an assertion - the reviewer's claim that os.access would validate the test's own wrong path and hide the mismatch is false. The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive: both derivations predate fd41ca3 (the pre-fix test declared PLUGIN_ROOT and LAUNCHER the same way).

In the pre-fd41ca3 code 'breached()' returned 'tokens >= ceiling and not finalized and not hook.agent_id' and gate returned None when not breached, so the compliant close-out path emitted nothing; deleting finalize_invoked for F1 made stop_hook_active the only signal, and the surviving message 'this session was NOT closed out' then fired on exactly the success path. The agent declined the proposed transcript re-check (it is the matcher F1 rejected) and made the message conditional instead.
guidance_note: When a fix deletes a signal, re-read every message and comment whose truth depended on it - the deletion changes which path each remaining branch is reached by.

evidence: Both halves of the flagged line ('open(transcript_path, rb).read()') were introduced by fd41ca3, which deleted the seek-based window for F4. The unclosed handle is real and was fixed with Path.read_bytes; the streaming half is not - the agent measured 32ms on a live 2.6MB transcript for a hook that runs once per turn, and re-adding the window would restore the code F1 and F4 both found bugs in.
guidance_note: State the cost model beside a deleted optimization (once per turn, 32ms) so the next reviewer or the next scope change can see when the answer flips.

evidence: This is a regression the rewrite introduced: the pre-fd41ca3 test asserted 'each event runs the mode this file tests' by checking 'context-ceiling.py\" {mode}' appeared in each registered command, and the fd41ca3 patch deletes that check along with the mode argv, leaving only 'list(registered) == [Stop]'. The agent restored a stronger form (basename of HOOK plus ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} in the command) and checked three concrete cases against it.
guidance_note: When a rewrite deletes an assertion because the thing it asserted about changed shape, re-express the assertion for the new shape in the same commit instead of dropping it.

evidence: stop_hook_active is Claude Code's transcript-wide flag, so the comment fd41ca3 added ('stop_hook_active is true only on a stop this hook already blocked') is false as written; the underlying edge case predates the fix but the assertion about it did not. The agent removed the comment and declined a self-tracked marker file, which is defensible once F6's fix made the message true in that scenario too.
guidance_note: A comment that asserts an exclusive property of a harness-provided flag is a claim about someone else's contract - state what the flag means and what the code assumes, separately.

evidence: This is the same defect as F3, raised again a round later: F3 named two unquoted interpolations (the PostToolUse additionalContext and the gate block reason), fd41ca3 removed the PostToolUse arm for unrelated reasons and left the block reason, and both were finally quoted in b0fb825. The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive in the causal sense - the defect survived the fix commit rather than being created by it.
guidance_note: Land the fix for every open finding before pushing the commit that triggers the next review round; a finding left unfixed on a new head is re-reported at the full price of a round.

evidence: The reviewer's mechanism is wrong: the agent walked a live daemon-hosted tree and found the chain intact and five hops deep (20487 -> 20437 bg-pty-host -> 20366 daemon run -> 21733 -> pane %6 shell), so the walk never hits pid 1 early. The finding's other half - that the premise was unverified and untested - was right, and the agent published a merge-blocker claim built on the tracking ticket's topology before retracting it 23 minutes later. The flag is a false positive: b0fb825 touched only context-ceiling.py and its test, while _discover_tmux_pane came from the unrelated d8b8e0f.
guidance_note: Verify a ticket's asserted process topology against the live system before publishing a merge blocker built on it - the retracted blocker cost more than the finding did.

evidence: _discover_tmux_pane decides where a handoff is pasted and which process is reset, and it shipped with no test; the agent conceded the point twice and its own wrong-then-retracted analysis on the sibling thread is direct evidence that a test would have answered it faster. Resolution was a tracked ticket (promptctl-finalize-hrm) deferred past merge by owner decision, not a fix. Flag is a false positive - the function came from d8b8e0f, not from the named fix commit b0fb825.
guidance_note: New side-effecting logic (spawns, kills, pastes into a terminal) needs its test in the commit that adds it, especially when that commit is unrelated scope added to an in-review PR.

evidence: The snapshot from 'tmux list-panes -a' is taken once before a walk that re-queries 'ps -o ppid=' per hop, so a recycled pid can match a pane the process never descended from - the race is real as described, and its failure mode (a handoff pasted into an unrelated terminal that is then reset) is worse than the return-1 fallback. Deferred to promptctl-finalize-hrm with the fix direction recorded (compare ps -o lstart= alongside the pid). Flag is a false positive: the code came from d8b8e0f, not b0fb825.
guidance_note: A match built on pid identity needs something a recycled pid cannot forge (start time) at the time it is written, not after a reviewer names the race.

narrative: Round 0 found four real issues in the hook; the agent answered three of them with one large deletion commit (fd41ca3, -342/+63 in the hook) and did not fix the fourth (F3, the unquoted launcher path) before pushing. Round 1 was therefore paid for twice: three of its six findings (F6, F8, F9) are defects the deletion introduced - a message that now fires on the compliant path, a registration assertion the test rewrite silently dropped, and a comment asserting a property stop_hook_active does not have - and a fourth (F10) is F3 re-reported. Round 2 exists almost entirely for d8b8e0f, an unrelated tmux-pane-discovery feature pushed onto the branch mid-review, whose three findings all ended as deferred tickets. The pushbacks (F5, F7, F11) were all checked against code or a live process tree and all held, though F11's first reply published a merge blocker that had to be retracted.
guidance_observations: A large delete-and-rewrite answer to a review is the highest-risk fix shape here: it closed three findings and created three new ones, all of which were assertions or messages whose truth depended on what was deleted.
Pushing an unrelated feature onto a PR that is mid-review bought a whole extra review round whose entire yield was deferred to a follow-up ticket.
The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag fired on all six round-1 and all three round-2 findings, but three of those nine are false positives - the flag tracks the round head, not what the commit touched.

evidence: The premise holds on all three counts: segments() classified by the first word only, so 'git commit -m \"$(...)\"' passed while the shell ran the substitution, and the launcher matched by basename while git matched the literal string. The agent inverted the parser in 36da072 (prove-plain rather than blocklist), which was the better of the two offered fixes - but I checked 36da072 and it does not touch the launcher/git matching at all, and the reply never mentions that half of the finding.
guidance_note: A finding that names two independent defects needs two answers in the reply; the unanswered launcher/git asymmetry here came back as F5 and again as F9, costing two further rounds.

evidence: shlex's default whitespace set swallows a bare newline, so 'git status\nrm -rf /tmp/important' tokenized to one segment whose first word is git and was permitted while bash ran two commands - a full bypass, correctly described. The agent made newline a separator and, more usefully, replaced the operator enumeration with the character set '&|;\n' so operators nobody listed also end a segment.
guidance_note: Write the accept/reject shape table before writing a matcher over a grammar you do not own: an enumerated separator list for shell was guaranteed to be short by one, and it was short by three.

evidence: Wiring context_tokens to PreToolUse turned a once-per-turn whole-file read into a per-tool-call one on a transcript the module's own docstring says reaches 909k tokens over 757 calls; the agent took the seek-from-tail option and declined the mtime cache because the transcript is appended to between the call and the hook. Worth noting across PRs: this is the same whole-file read the agent declined to change in laws#21/F7 on a measurement that was valid only for the once-per-turn scope it then left behind.
guidance_note: When moving existing logic onto a hotter event, re-run the measurement that justified its current shape - the cost argument recorded in the earlier PR was scope-bound and the scope changed.

evidence: With punctuation_chars=True shlex emits '|&' as one token that is absent from OPERATORS, so it was appended as a literal word and 'git status |& rm -rf /tmp/important' passed as a single git segment - the third instance of the same enumeration gap as F1 and F2, fixed by the same character-set rewrite in 36da072.
guidance_note: Three findings in one round sampling one cause is the signal to stop patching instances and change the shape - which the agent did, but only after the reviewer supplied the third sample.

evidence: Permitting any git subcommand above the ceiling let a thrashing session run 'git reset --hard' or 'git clean -xdf' and destroy the uncommitted work the handoff exists to carry, which is the gate defeating its own purpose; the agent narrowed to status/diff/log/show/rev-parse/add/commit/push, dropped branch, and required the subcommand to be the second word. The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a causal false positive: 0210886 (01:47) predates the F1 fix 36da072 (02:05), so this round reviewed a head where F1's launcher-matching half was still unfixed and re-raised it alongside a genuinely new destructive-subcommand finding.
guidance_note: Do not push unrelated commits while a review round is outstanding - the next round re-reviews a head that still contains every unfixed finding, and you pay for the duplicates.

evidence: Same defect as F3 and closed by the same commit (36da072); the reviewer re-derived it because round 1 ran against 0210886, pushed before that fix landed. The premise itself is correct for the same reason F3's is.
guidance_note: Duplicate findings across rounds are a scheduling defect, not a reviewer defect - the fix commit and the reply have to land before the next push.

evidence: Restates F1's command-substitution bypass and adds redirection ('git status > /some/file'), both true of the code at 0210886; the reviewer's closing sentence - do not fabricate a security boundary out of a partial tokenizer - is the fix the agent actually took, and the agent says so. Again a duplicate raised on a pre-fix head rather than a consequence of a fix.

Two raw subprocess.run calls bypassed the run() helper that clears MEMENTO_CONTEXT_CEILING and points MEMENTO_CEILING_FILE at a tempdir, and CEILING = resolve_ceiling() runs at import, so a developer of this plugin - the likeliest person to have a real ceiling file - would see both assertions fail for an unrelated reason. The agent extracted a shared isolated() helper rather than copying the env into both call sites. Not caused by a fix: resolve_ceiling came from 0ba4b4b5, an unrelated mid-review commit.
guidance_note: Environment isolation belongs in one helper the first time a second call site appears, not after a reviewer finds the site that skipped it.

evidence: I read the 9c41bda patch: it added 'return os.path.realpath(part[0]) == os.path.realpath(LAUNCHER)' for the launcher and left 'if part[0] == \"git\"' literal, so the asymmetry F1 named in round 0 and F5 re-raised in round 1 was half-fixed and came back a third time. The agent's different fix is right and I checked its reasoning: '/usr/bin/git' and the Homebrew git are different files, so resolving git the way the launcher is resolved would bless whichever one PATH names and deny every other real git.
guidance_note: When a finding names an asymmetry between two matchers, decide and record the answer for both sides in the same commit - even 'these two ask different questions, deliberately' closes the thread instead of re-opening it twice.

evidence: 'misquoted = LAUNCHER in command' matched any command merely mentioning the path, so 'cat <launcher>' was answered with 'this IS the close-out ... rewrite it and run it again'. Two hops of cause: the strict prove-plain parser from 36da072 (F1's fix) trapped a live session, whose commit message (6604003) records it spending two denials and ~10k tokens on a heredoc, and the MISQUOTED coaching added to mitigate that is what carries this bug. The agent replaced the second derivation with one classify() call rather than patching the predicate.
guidance_note: A tightened parser needs its refusal message designed in the same change - the strict parser shipped without a way to say 'permitted, but not spelled that way', and the retrofit cost a round.

evidence: The reviewer flagged its own reachability caveat and the agent resolved it in the reviewer's favour by pulling a real transcript (523b97e3): a PreToolUse-denied call is recorded as an ordinary tool_use, so launched() said a refused close-out had run and Stop let the session end with no handoff. The agent declined the proposed fix (re-derive is_closeout) with two concrete counterexamples and instead read is_error off the recorded tool_result, which also covers a launcher that ran and failed. Not caused by a review fix: launched() came from dff50d4, a live-session-driven commit.
guidance_note: Prefer reading an outcome from where the system already records it over recomputing it from the input that produced it - the recomputation diverges in both directions.

evidence: os.environ.get returns '' for an exported-empty variable, which is neither in DISABLED nor isdigit(), so parse_ceiling called sys.exit at import - and by this module's own documented semantics a non-zero exit is a non-blocking error, i.e. the ceiling silently stops being enforced. The file branch already had the '.strip()' guard the env branch lacked; the agent extracted one configured() predicate both sources call rather than copying the guard.
guidance_note: Two sources feeding one setting need one predicate for 'is this configured at all' the first time the second source is added; the file branch and the env branch agreed by coincidence until they did not.

evidence: The agent demonstrated the premise rather than reasoning about it: the new assertion did not merely fail, it took the whole suite down with 'TypeError: object of type NoneType has no len()' at the reviewer's line number. The crashing read is in the original commit; what the reviewer used to spot it - a second, differently-guarded read of the same field - came from 6604003, so this is not a consequence of any fix. Fixed by construction (one classify() read of 'get(command) or \"\"') rather than by matching spellings.
guidance_note: Two reads of the same external field in one module is the defect, independent of whether the null case is reachable - collapse them rather than making the guards match.

evidence: The factual half is true - permitted git subcommands take arbitrary arguments, so 'git diff --output=<path>' is not refused - but the escalation framing is wrong, and I verified the decisive fact in the merged hook: pretool() returns 'label, None' for a permitted call and only ever emits permissionDecision deny, so the gate can subtract capability and never grant it, and every command named is equally runnable below the ceiling where the hook does nothing. The surface being probed is the GIT_SUBCOMMANDS allowlist F5's fix introduced.
guidance_note: Write the threat model into the module docstring at design time, as this one did - it is what let a security-framed finding be answered in one reply instead of a fix.

evidence: Claude Code dispatches parallel tool calls in one turn and each fires its own hook process, so the exists/stat then write_text truncation then separate open('a') append sequence races exactly as described - two processes can both truncate, or a truncate can land between another's open and write. The agent collapsed all three steps onto one flock-held handle with the size read via fstat, and mutation-checked the new truncation test. The log came from 0210886 and the concurrency from this PR's own PreToolUse arm, not from a fix.
guidance_note: A file written by a per-tool-call hook is a multi-writer resource from the first line - the check-truncate-append sequence needed the lock when it was written, not when the event it runs on got hotter.

evidence: git's ext:: remote helper does run an arbitrary command, so the mechanism is real, but the same deny-only fact settles it: the permitted call gets no hook output and proceeds through Claude Code's ordinary permission system, identical to the flow below the ceiling, so this gate is not the boundary the RCE crosses. segments()' own docstring pre-states the scope ('which tools run, not what a trusted tool is then asked to do'), which is what makes the pushback checkable rather than assertive.

narrative: Five rounds and $13.93 of review for one hook. Round 0 found a real class of parser bypass and the agent's answer - invert the parser to prove a command plain - was the right shape and closed three findings at once. Two things then cost three more rounds. First, the agent kept pushing unrelated commits while a round was outstanding (three between round 0 and round 1, two more between rounds 1 and 2), so round 1 re-reported F1's and F3's defects on a head where their fixes had not landed. Second, F1 named the launcher/git matching asymmetry in its second paragraph, the reply never addressed it, the F5 fix closed only the launcher half, and it came back as F9 in round 2 - one defect, three rounds. The two S4 pushbacks in round 3 were both correct and both cheap, because the module docstring had already stated the threat model in writing.
guidance_observations: The single largest cost driver in this PR is pushing new commits onto a branch with unaddressed review findings; four of round 1's four findings were either duplicates or issues in the commits pushed since round 0.
Findings with more than one claim in them are systematically under-answered - the reply addresses the headline and drops the rest, and the dropped part returns at full round cost.

Live-session evidence was the agent's strongest instrument here (a real transcript settled F11's reachability, a real bash PATH-shim suite would have caught all of round 0), and it was used only after the reviewer asked.
Every accepted fix in rounds 2 and 3 was mutation-checked against the pre-fix code, which is why round 4 found nothing - that discipline is worth naming in guidance.

evidence: SKILL.md claims 'the only genuine failure is a machine with no tmux binary at all and no iTerm2 to fall back to either' while the detached branch adds two more exit-2 paths (_find_claude_pid finding no ancestor, 'command -v claude' failing); the agent confirmed both and volunteered a third that the F4 fix would add. Only the plan was posted - the PR was closed unmerged on 2026-08-25 when main was hard-reset after an unrelated incident, and the work was restored via laws#27.
guidance_note: A doc sentence that enumerates failure modes is a claim that goes stale the moment a branch adds an exit path - update it in the commit that adds the path.

evidence: The ready-timeout arm exits 1 without killing the tmux session it just created, and it deliberately leaves the old process alive, so a session that came up but missed the banner match becomes a second live agent that nothing names except a tempfile log. The agent accepted and tightened the proposal, refusing the reviewer's '|| true' so a failed kill is logged rather than swallowed. Plan only - the PR was closed unmerged.
guidance_note: A failure path that returns after creating a resource must destroy it in the same edit; the create and its cleanup are one thought, not two.

evidence: About eight assertions depend on _find_claude_pid finding a real claude-named ancestor of the test runner, which the suite's own docstring admits holds only 'for how this suite is actually run (inside Claude Code)' - in CI or a plain shell they return DECLINED and fail on correct code. The agent's plan interposes a fixture process named claude above the nest chain, which also preserves the depth-bound cases. Plan only - the PR was closed unmerged.
guidance_note: A suite whose docstring admits it depends on how it is launched has already found the bug; synthesize the ancestor rather than documenting the coupling.

evidence: The iTerm2 arm is a conjunction ending in a live osascript probe, so a user inside iTerm2 whose Automation permission is not yet granted falls through to the new detached arm, which then finds the visible claude process, stands up a hidden tmux session and kills the terminal the user is looking at - strictly worse than the graceful decline this case produced before the PR, with the real fault never named. The agent took the reviewer's second option and made the claimed-but-unprobeable case exit 2 with the Automation cause named. Plan only - the PR was closed unmerged.
guidance_note: A new fallback arm must distinguish 'the previous arm has no surface' from 'the previous arm's capability probe failed'; sharing one else-branch turns a broken permission into a destroyed session.

evidence: The tmux and iTerm2 parentheticals both state their effect on the current process ('reset the pane in place', 'kill the running claude and relaunch it fresh') while the new detached one omits that it SIGTERMs and then SIGKILLs the process invoking it, leaving the bash header comment as the only place that says so. The agent agreed and planned the retire clause. Plan only - the PR was closed unmerged.
guidance_note: When adding an item to a doc list, match the facts its siblings already state - an omission in a parallel list reads as an absence of the behavior.

evidence: The suite drives the launcher only in FINALIZE_DRY_RUN, so it covers transport selection and none of the ~90 new lines that create a tmux session, poll for a banner, re-issue a carried goal and kill the old process; the agent accepted and specified three real-tmux cases against a private TMUX_TMPDIR server, plus making the timing constants overridable so the failure paths do not cost 40s each. Plan only - the PR was closed unmerged.
guidance_note: Dry-run tests prove which branch was chosen, never what the branch does - side-effecting workers need a real fixture harness in the commit that adds them.

narrative: One review round, six findings, all correct and all accepted - but only as plans, posted about 28 hours after the review and roughly an hour before the PR was closed. The findings themselves are the strongest set in this batch: F4 in particular identifies that the new detached transport turns a first-run macOS Automation-permission failure into 'the user's visible terminal is killed and replaced by a hidden one', which is a worse outcome than the decline the code had before the PR. Nothing was implemented here; the PR was closed unmerged on 2026-08-25 when main was hard-reset after a session ran a server-wide tmux kill, and the work was restored in laws#27. Separately, the PR body still asserts that a daemon-hosted session's ancestry walk resolves to the spawner's pane - the exact claim the same agent had retracted two days earlier on laws#21/F11.
guidance_observations: Every finding in this round is about a new branch's edges - a fallback that fires on a broken probe, a failure path that leaks what it created, a doc list whose new entry omits what its siblings state - which is what a new-arm checklist would catch before review.

The plan-only reply pattern (six 'Plan: valid' posts with no implementation) leaves every thread open and produces no evidence; here it was overtaken by events, but it is indistinguishable from work that was never done.
A design premise retracted on one PR was still driving the design of the next PR two days later, because the retraction lived in a review thread and the ticket it corrected was never updated.
